title: fix(devx): name a remedy a peer's reader can perform in the root bound's refusal
body:
Fixes #8059

## Not a rule change — the rule is ratified unchanged

`scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs` maps third-party specifiers from `dependencies`
**only**, never `peerDependencies`, never `devDependencies`. That is deliberate, documented
in the file's own header, and fails **closed**; triage ratified it unchanged and this PR does
not widen it by a byte. The `resolvesOnlyThroughRootManifest` predicate, the two enforcement
points and the four self-controls are untouched.

What changes is **the text the refusal prints**.

## The defect

Four packages declare `react-router-dom` as a peer and none as a dependency — re-measured on
this PR's base `f76f43628`, not taken from the card's `58cd01a38`:

| package | peerDependencies | in dependencies |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `packages/app-shell` | `^6.0.0 \|\| ^7.0.0` | no |
| `packages/layout` | `^6.0.0 \|\| ^7.0.0` | no |
| `packages/plugin-designer` | `^6.0.0 \|\| ^7.0.0` | no |
| `packages/plugin-detail` | `^6.0.0 \|\| ^7.0.0` | no |

The repository root declares it in `devDependencies` (`^7.18.2`), so the root bound refuses any
covered block importing it. On those four pages the refusal named two remedies and **neither
fits the case it actually fires on**:

1. *"Import what an imported package DECLARES"* reads as **impossible**, because the package
   **does** declare it — in a field this map does not read. Parsing the sentence correctly
   required already knowing that, which is knowledge the message itself withheld.
2. *"declare the block a fragment"* stops the **whole** block compiling, the documented
   package's own surface included. On `packages/layout/README.md` that surrenders the
   `AppShell` / `SidebarNav` composition — which is exactly where objectui#3999 and
   objectui#4817 both landed defects.

A refusal is a contract with its reader. One whose named remedy cannot be performed, and whose
fallback deletes coverage the reader wanted, is the *declared-but-not-enforced* shape wearing a
message's clothes.

## The third shape, which neither the message nor the header named

Stand the peer's bindings in with `declare const` typed to what the block uses them as, and
import only what the package declares in its `dependencies`. The block still compiles, so the
documented composition around it stays genuinely checked. It is already worked in-tree, at
`packages/layout/README.md` under "Usage with React Router".

So the refusal now:

- qualifies "declares" with the field it means, and says why a peer is not that field;
- names the stand-in shape together with the property that earns it (the block still compiles);
- keeps the fragment remedy but **ranks it last, with its cost stated** — it is the one that
  deletes coverage.

The same remedy is added to the `dependencies` only header bullet, so rule and message cannot
drift apart.

## Non-vacuity — the message is shown PRINTED, not merely present in the source

A message change can assert nothing, so the failing case was constructed: the `declare const`
stand-ins in `packages/layout/README.md` were replaced by a real
`import { BrowserRouter, Routes, Route } from 'react-router-dom';`. The mutation was proved on
disk by blob hash and by anchored marker counts in both directions **before** the gate ran, and
restored under an `EXIT INT TERM` trap; the restore is proved by state (`git diff HEAD` empty,
hash back to the HEAD blob), never by an exit code.

Before (`node scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs`, exit 1):

```
  [bound]     packages/layout/README.md:201  imports 'react-router-dom', which resolve only
through this repository's ROOT package.json — this workspace's own devDependency set, not
anything a reader of the documented packages installs. Import what an imported package
DECLARES, or declare the block a fragment with a reason naming what the reader must install:
                (the fragment marker example)
```

After (same construction, same exit 1):

```
  [bound]     packages/layout/README.md:201  imports 'react-router-dom', which resolve only
through this repository's ROOT package.json — this workspace's own devDependency set, not
anything a reader of the documented packages installs. Import what an imported package
declares in its `dependencies`. A `peerDependencies` entry is a declaration too, but not one
this map reads: a peer is a requirement ON the reader, which may be unmet.
                If the specifier IS such a peer and this block needs its bindings, stand them
in with `declare const` typed to what the block uses them as, and import only what the package
declares. The block still compiles, so the documented package's own surface around it stays
checked — worked example: `packages/layout/README.md`, under "Usage with React Router".
                Declaring the block a fragment is the LAST resort: it stops the WHOLE block
compiling, that package's own surface included, so reach for it only when the block cannot
compile for reasons a stand-in cannot supply. Its reason must name what the reader installs:
                (the fragment marker example)
```

Both runs printed `Root bound:     1 block(s) ... and were NOT semantically checked.`

## Nothing pinned a word of this diagnostic — which is how it drifted

`git grep` over the whole tree found the two remedy sentences in **one** place: the gate source
itself. No test asserted any of it. A diagnostic nothing pins drifts silently, so this PR adds
the pin, in the `ROOT BOUND ... in this repository` block that already pins the rule's header.

Reverse verification, from the committed state: restoring the OLD remedy sentence in the gate
(mutation proved on disk by hash and marker counts, `node --check` on the ablated source,
restore proved by `git diff HEAD` empty) turns the new pin **red** —
`AssertionError: expected '#!/usr/bin/env node...' to contain 'a peer is a requirement ON the reader'`,
`Tests 1 failed | 100 passed`. Predicted direction was "turns red"; that is what was observed.

## The fence, re-derived rather than taken

The bound message is inside the region after the `── Fence scanning` banner. That region is
licensed by `scripts/__tests__/check-doc-example-types.test.ts:373`, and the licence is
`check-doc-example-types`' own card's, not this one's. Re-derived on this base:

- the banner is at `:945`, the bound message at `:2623` (post-change), the header bullet at
  `:341` — **before** the banner, outside the region entirely;
- the pin asserts exactly two substrings after the banner, `export function scanFences(source)`
  and `export function compileSnippets(`. This diff touches neither signature;
- no test in the repository hashes this gate: `createHash` 0 hits, `sha256` 0 hits. Control on
  the same file so the zeros are readings: `check-doc-snippet-types` 7 hits, `describe(` 18 hits;
- `scripts/__tests__/check-doc-example-types.test.ts` passes, 46/46, including that licence pin.

## Verification

Base `f76f43628`. All exit codes captured before any pipe (`cmd > file 2>&1; EXIT=$?`), and the
gate verdicts quoted from the gates' own printed lines.

- `pnpm check:doc-snippets` — exit 0 before and after: *"Every covered documentation snippet
  compiles against the built types."* 244 documents scanned, 632 of 632 blocks judged, 0 failed.
- `node scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs --build-filter` exit 0, `--emit-census` exit 0 (the
  two other modes `doc-snippet-types.yml` runs).
- `pnpm check:doc-examples` exit 0, `pnpm check:doc-example-readers` exit 0 — the sibling gates
  that import this harness.
- `scripts/__tests__/` in full: **120 of 121 files pass, 3630 tests**. The one failure is
  `check-lint-rule-coverage.test.ts`, and it is **not this diff's**: it walks the filesystem
  filtered by eslint ignores rather than by git, so the untracked build output
  `apps/console/plugin.js` (produced by this workspace's own `pnpm build`, gitignored at
  `apps/console/.gitignore:16`) reads as an unledgered file. Moving that artifact aside turns
  the same file green 27/27 with no other change. Already filed as objectui#8369, which is open.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` — **run, not guessed**: exit 0, *"No source or
  published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed."*
  2 files changed, 0 of them published source. No `skip-changeset` label applied: in this repo
  that label exempts nothing, and the gate's verdict line is the authority.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on both paths — exit 0,
  *"NOT GOVERNED — 2 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched."*
- `pnpm exec turbo ls --affected` against the base: **0 packages**. The diff is entirely under
  `scripts/`, so the owed suite is the tooling one above, not a package's `test`/`typecheck`.
- Lint: the **whole-repo union** `pnpm exec eslint . --no-inline-config --format json`, run at
  the final commit `139b6a001` on a clean tree — no narrowing, so no narrowing needs excusing.
  Population read from eslint's own config: **4503 files**. Both files this PR touches are in
  that population at **0 errors, 0 warnings**. The repository's 94 errors / 12430 warnings are
  carried by 78 other files this diff does not touch.
- Control bytes: `grep -naP` for the C0/C1 set over both touched files returns nothing (exit 1),
  with a control term present in the same files to prove the read.

## Scope

Two files, both under `scripts/`. Deliberately **not** touched, and why:

- the `dependencies`-only mapping itself — ratified unchanged by triage, and widening it is what
  this card explicitly is not;
- `scripts/check-doc-example-types.mjs:1289`, whose `[bound]` line is a ledger reason string in
  a gate with no fragment-marker remedy at all — a different remedy model, not the same defect;
- the emitted-code census's own `[bound]` line, which fires today on `react-router-dom` in
  `packages/cli/src/utils/app-generator.ts`. That path is report-only and objectui#7864 rules
  that its disposition is decided on a follow-up card and not here.

Drafted by the `domain:devx @ objectui` os-dev seat, session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`,
on base `f76f43628`.
